steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Britain's geology is remarkably diverse for its size, with rocks ranging from the Archean (Lewisian Gneiss, ~3 billion years) to recent Holocene deposits | Key Fact: The Scottish Highlands contain the oldest rocks: Lewisian Gneiss (Precambrian), overlain by Torridon Sandstone and Moine Schists | Key Fact: The Lake District has Ordovician and Silurian volcanic and sedimentary rocks, deformed during the Caledonian orogeny | Key Fact: The Pennines are a Carboniferous limestone and millstone grit anticline, formed by the Variscan orogeny

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from geology of britain, and one past-paper question.
